questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How atomic clocks work
Different attitudes to being on time
How to plan a busy working day
Why meetings often start late
questions.why: Neil says they are discussing people's attitudes to being on time and how important punctuality is.

questions.q: Why does Catherine say she doesn't like to arrive early?
options: She is always stuck in traffic
She thinks it is rude
She has too many deadlines
She doesn't want to wait around for Neil
questions.why: Catherine says she doesn't want to be early and then wait around for Neil.

questions.q: According to Grace Pacie, what is typical of a 'time bender'?
options: They don't want to be late but don't allow enough time
They are always early for everything
They deliberately arrive late to look important
They never turn up to meetings
questions.why: She says they don't want to be late but resist being early and don't allow enough time.

questions.q: What is Catherine's attitude to deadlines?
options: She misses most of them because she is too busy
She always finishes everything well before it's due
She meets key ones but doesn't stress about small things
She asks for more time for every single deadline
questions.why: She says if a deadline really matters she'll make it, but less important things aren't worth the stress.

questions.q: How does Neil feel about being late?
options: Relaxed, because most things start late
Anxious, so he always arrives early
Embarrassed, but it happens often
He doesn't mind if others are late
questions.why: Neil says being late makes him anxious, which is why he always arrives early.

questions.q: According to Philippa Perry, why might some people fear being early?
options: They don't want to stand out and feel awkward alone
They think it wastes time
They don't like the people they are meeting
They worry about getting lost
questions.why: She mentions a fear of being conspicuous, standing out, having no one to talk to and feeling awkward.

questions.q: Which reason does Catherine say explains her own lateness?
options: She is afraid of standing out
She has no one to talk to when she arrives
She forgets what time things start
She thinks there is time to fit everything in
questions.why: She says it's the other reason Perry mentioned: 'I just think there's time to pack everything in!'

questions.q: What advice from the Woman's Hour experts does Neil repeat?
options: Buy a more accurate watch
Always leave an hour early
Decide to be on time instead of trying
Stop making so many appointments
questions.why: Neil says you shouldn't 'try' to be on time, you should 'decide' to be on time.
